verdicts.slides: carries a proved law into another proved law; link checked along the dial
verdicts.plausible: numbers slide, the law in between is not proved here
verdicts.partly: survives on part of the dial, breaks on the rest
verdicts.disguise: the move is really another dial
verdicts.no: no slide (another dial, or does not depend on q)

rows.law: Core law o_k: order free, identity 0, the wall
rows.reason: Over q-commuting inputs o_k stays associative (A1); order gap k(1-q)ab (A2): order-free at q = 1 (Lean circK_comm), exclusion at q = -1 (Lean anticommute_self_zero, pauli)

rows.law: Corner expansion: 1 + (x1 o ... o xn) = sum over corners
rows.reason: Run the chain in reversed order over x_j x_i = q x_i x_j: rank-m corners get q^C(m,2) (B1), the soliton corner form (Lean tau3_equal_corner); sorted order keeps the plain expansion (B2)
(x + y)^n with yx = q xy is the q-binomial (Potter 1950, Schutzenberger 1953; C1); q = 1 binomial (Lean gauss_at_one), q = 0 sorted words, q -> inf reversed word, roots of unity q-Lucas
Rungs live on the half-line and the k dial; no product of two moves to reorder
Jackson's q-derivative gives [n]_q x^(n-1) (L4), but its q = 1 + h is a step size: the k dial

rows.law: Plane law (k, d): circle, parabola, hyperbola
rows.reason: The face weight q = beta/alpha is a reading of (k, d): (1+q)^2/q = k^2/d (L1); turning it is turning d (curvature dial in disguise)
Elements that square to numbers allow only q = +1 or -1 (I1, order-dial G1); in between, Clifford breaks
The Tate parameter q of the torus (QDial tate_glue_n) is the curve's period, not a swap factor
Velocity addition is a ball law on the plane dial; no q
Bayes in odds form is commutative and has no swap factor

rows.law: Swap rule: turn = d x area (Thomas, Foucault, pulsars)
rows.reason: Turn = d x area flattens into phase = area/hbar with hbar = 1/(j d) (quantum-action A3): the d dial and spin, not q at fixed d

rows.law: Maxwell as one equation, F as a wedge
rows.reason: Maxwell's law does not depend on q (magnetic translations obey a Weyl rule, but that is not proved here)
Einstein tensor: no swap factor
Causal-diamond counting: no swap factor
Routes through the cube (the permutohedron's vertices) weighted q^inv sum to [n]_q! (F1; cube-weights E1): n! at q = 1, one route at q = 0, all cancel at a cube root of 1 from n = 3 (F2)
q-Catalan and q-Stirling numbers exist in print (Carlitz) but are not built in this repo
[n]_q = sum over words with one y of q^inv (D1): n at q = 1, 1 at q = 0, parity at q = -1, 0 at a root of unity (Lean QDial); same numbers as the k dial at k = q - 1 (Lean qnum_lift)
Face weights q^area: inversions = path area (E2), sum = [n,m]_q (E1): counts C(n,m) at q = 1 (Lean gauss_at_one), keeps the one minimum at q -> 0 (E3; Lean theta2_face, orbit_product_q0)
Toric point counts run through a = q - 1 points on the circle (Lean fan_count): q is the field size, reached through the k dial
Jones polynomial: Lean proves t = 1 (components) and t = -1 (determinant); t = e^{2pi i/3} and t = i checked (J2, J3); that t is the order dial goes through U_q(sl2), not proved here
The union rule is the k dial at k = -1

rows.law: Logistic (independent yes/no) and softmax (one of many)
rows.reason: Logistic and softmax are commutative sums
Tsallis's q is k + 1 (the homothety dial), the first clashing meaning of q, not the order dial
Shannon and code lengths: commutative
Repeats survive only at q = 1; any q != 1 on self-swaps forces x^2 = 0 (I2, Lean anticommute_self_zero): Bose to Fermi is a jump; anyons in between not proved
